eudoxus.name: Eudoxus of Cnidus

hilbert.name: David Hilbert
hilbert.bio: Author of Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899), reorganizing Euclidean geometry into five rigorous axiom groups (incidence, order, congruence, parallels, continuity) and proving the theory of plane area independent of continuity.

playfair.name: John Playfair
playfair.bio: Popularized 'Playfair's Axiom' (already stated by Proclus) as a modern substitute for Euclid's Fifth Postulate in his Elements of Geometry (1795).

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras of Samos
pythagoras.bio: Transformed geometry into a liberal philosophical science; credited with the discovery of the theory of proportions, the application of areas (Book II), the theorem on the right-angled triangle (I.47), and the construction of the cosmic figures.

riemann.bio: In his 1854 Habilitationsschrift, generalized geometry to n-dimensional manifolds of variable curvature, distinguishing unboundedness from infinitude and introducing spherical/elliptic non-Euclidean geometry.

simplicius.name: Simplicius of Cilicia
simplicius.bio: Preserved Eudemus's verbatim account of the quadrature of lunes by Hippocrates of Chios (in his Commentary on Aristotle's Physics) and ancient proofs of the Parallel Postulate (in an-Nairīzī).
works: Commentary on the Premises of Euclid's Elements
In Aristotelis Physicorum Libros Commentaria (ed. Diels)

simson.name: Robert Simson
simson.role: Professor of Mathematics at the University of Glasgow
simson.bio: Published the critical Latin and English edition of Books I–VI, XI, and XII of Euclid's Elements (1756) that served as the standard textbook in the English-speaking world for over a century.

thales.name: Thales of Miletus
thales.role: Ionion Natural Philosopher & Pioneer of Greek Geometry
thales.bio: Introduced geometry from Egypt into Greece; credited by Eudemus and Proclus with propositions I.5, I.15, I.26, and the theorem that the angle in a semicircle is a right angle (III.31).

theaetetus.name: Theaetetus of Athens
theaetetus.bio: Developed the general classification of incommensurable magnitudes (medial, binomial, apotome) codified in Book X and completed the theoretical construction of the five regular solids (octahedron and icosahedron) in Book XIII.

theodorus-of-cyrene.name: Theodorus of Cyrene
theodorus-of-cyrene.role: Pythagorean Geometer; Teacher of Plato and Theaetetus
theodorus-of-cyrene.bio: Proved the irrationality of the square roots of non-square integers from 3 up to 17 (Plato, Theaetetus 147D).

theodosius.name: Theodosius
theodosius.bio: Historical mathematician, philosopher, commentator, or modern scholar cited in Heath's edition of Euclid's Elements.

theon-of-alexandria.name: Theon of Alexandria
theon-of-alexandria.role: Alexandrian Editor of Euclid's Elements; Father of Hypatia
theon-of-alexandria.bio: Produced the standard late-antique recension of Euclid's Elements that dominated all Greek manuscripts until Peyrard's discovery of the non-Theonine Vatican manuscript (P = Vat. gr. 190).

theon-of-smyrna.name: Theon of Smyrna
theon-of-smyrna.bio: Author of an exposition of arithmetic, music, and astronomy useful for reading Plato, preserving the theory of side and diameter numbers (rational approximations to √2).
works: Expositio rerum mathematicarum ad legendum Platonem utilium
